title: slab-rebalance-eviction-healer-and-read-amplification-patch-for-gpu-oom-ramp
creator: Asha Menon
description: Customer escalations from three customers (hosted, dedicated, and private) observed an escalating GPU OOM waveform tied to sustained read-amplification in the KV layer and a page-writer starvation path. This ticket teams the short-term mitigations with a runtime patch that performs conservative slab rebalance, tombstone compaction, and an eviction-healer to limit per-session resident pages during heavy long-tail workloads.
impact_summary: Multiple customers reported sustained latency spikes followed by host-level GPU OOMs over 12-48h windows. Hosted customers experienced degraded throughput (>30% request failures) and dedicated/private customers saw degraded tail latency and occasional full-node evictions. Revenue and SLA risk elevated this to P0.
reproduction_steps: Replay customer trace A (s3://redwood-prod-traces/customer-A/2026-01-29) against a 8xA100 dedicated node with session pinning enabled
Run long-tail workload generator with 95th/99th percentile long context patterns (generator config: infra/tests/long_tail_gen.yaml) for 24 hours
Instrument KV profiler with --kv-sample-interval=250ms and run until slab-utilization divergent behavior observed
investigation_notes: Root cause: read-amplification from small random KV reads caused repeated page faults and prevented page-writer from making forward progress under heavy concurrent session allocations
KV tombstones accumulated because the background tombstone-compactor heuristic was reactive and deferred compaction when IO pressure was high, amplifying memory retention
Slab allocator skew: a hot-codepath caused small allocations to migrate into a dense slab without cross-slab rebalance, creating multi-tenant hot spots
Observed a race in session eviction logic where sessions marked for eviction could be re-pinned by long-running LRU refreshes, defeating eviction backpressure
mitigations_applied: Applied emergency config change: runtime flag --kv-eviction-threshold=0.65 on affected pools (rolled to hosted region us-west-2 and two dedicated clusters)
Enabled conservative tombstone compaction policy (--kv-compaction-pressure=high) to reclaim stale KV entries during IO pressure windows
Deployed session-sweeper backstop: background job 'session-evict-healer' (canary at 10% traffic) that force-evicts low-activity sessions when slab utilization > 70%
Added temporary customer-level rate limit for long-context generation flows (applied via route config) to reduce immediate pressure while patch was prepared
code_changes: runtime: introduce slab rebalance pass that migrates low-utilization slabs every N allocations (commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/commit/8b5f2c4)
kv: proactive tombstone compactor that triggers incremental compaction under read-amplification signatures (commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv/commit/3f1a9d2)
session: eviction healer that protects page-writer progress by preventing re-pin race (commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/session/commit/ea29b7f)
canary_plan: Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% across hosted clusters with monitoring checks at each step (5m stabilization window). Dedicated customers will get patch builds as hotfixes followed by coordinated reboots; private customers supplied patch bundle and upgrade instructions.
customer_updates: 2026-02-04: Initial alert + mitigation applied; asked customers to preserve logs and traces; promised 48h remediation ETA
2026-02-06: Shared canary plan and temporary route-level rate limits; invited customers to canary for dedicated clusters
2026-02-09: Post-canary update: metrics show 90% reduction in OOM spikes on canary hosts; plan to promote to full rollout after final validation
test_plan: Synthetic long-tail run for 72h with both 8xA100 and 4xA100 configs
Chaos test: random session eviction + network jitter to validate session-evict-healer robustness
Regression: run existing mem-leak/test-suite and compare slab util histograms pre/post patch
follow_up_actions: Schedule full postmortem with SRE and customer success (owner: Priya Singh) within one week of full rollout
Add telemetry for slab-migration events and tombstone-compaction latency to Console dashboards
Explore a long-term change: move to epoch-based allocation to reduce cross-session fragmentation (RFC to be drafted by runtime team)
Backfill runbooks for emergency knob --kv-eviction-threshold and make it visible in Console with recommended guardrails
notes: Edge case discovered: some private on-prem customers with older NV driver (470.x) had worse page-writer latencies; added note to upgrade matrix
We observed that turning on a previously dormant feature 'continuous-kv-prefetch' in one customer increased read-amplification; disabled for the customer and flagged as incompatible
Customer A provided an example mail thread and timeline: slack thread #cust-A-memory-escalation (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0456ABC/...)
communication_plan: Weekly cadence with impacted customers until postmortem complete; internal blameless review and RFC for allocator changes
release_notes: runtime-1.23: fix(kv): reduce read-amplification via proactive compactor; fix(runtime): slab rebalance and session eviction healer to mitigate GPU OOM cascades
